t: That no tract of land, nor any interest therein, which is hereafter purchased by the Secretary of the Interior with restricted funds by or for an Indian or Indians of the Five Civilized Tribes in Oklahoma of one-half or more Indian blood, enrolled or unenrolled, shall be construed to be restricted unless the deed conveying same shows upon its face that such purchase was made with restricted funds.

fable.w: The section only sets a rule of construction for when land purchased by the Secretary of the Interior for Indians of the Five Civilized Tribes is treated as restricted. The tempting reading is that the mention of Indians and tribes implies tribal involvement, but they appear only as beneficiaries of the purchases; no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is provided for any outside party.
fable.s: shall be construed to be restricted unless the deed conveying same shows upon its face that such purchase was made with restricted funds

qwen_block.w: This section establishes a legal condition for determining the status of land purchases (whether they are 'restricted' or not) based on the content of the deed. It does not require any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as tribes, states, or the public) before the Secretary makes a decision. The interaction described is purely administrative and legal regarding property titles.
qwen_block.s: That no tract of land, nor any interest therein, which is hereafter purchased by the Secretary of the Interior with restricted funds by or for an Indian or Indians of the Five Civilized Tribes in Oklahoma of one-half or more Indian blood, enrolled or unenrolled, shall be construed to be restricted unless the deed conveying same shows upon its face that such purchase was made with restricted funds.

opus.w: The section sets a rule for how land bought with restricted Indian funds is treated: it counts as restricted only if the deed says so on its face. It does not require consultation, a hearing, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue. The tribal members mentioned are buyers, or the people land is bought for, in a property transaction, not participants in a federal decision.
opus.s: shall be construed to be restricted unless the deed conveying same shows upon its face that such purchase was made with restricted funds
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section mentions Indians of the Five Civilized Tribes, who are outside the federal government. That fails here. The section only sets a rule for when land bought with restricted funds counts as restricted: the deed has to say so on its face. No outside party is consulted or coordinated with, and no one gets a right to sue or object. Buying land with restricted funds "by or for" an Indian is a property transaction, not a say in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a legal presumption regarding the status of land purchased with restricted funds. It does not require the Secretary of the Interior or any other federal official to consult with Indians, tribes, or any other outside parties before making a decision. The text is purely definitional and procedural regarding deed requirements.
qwen_chat.s: That no tract of land, nor any interest therein, which is hereafter purchased by the Secretary of the Interior with restricted funds by or for an Indian or Indians of the Five Civilized Tribes in Oklahoma of one-half or more Indian blood, enrolled or unenrolled, shall be construed to be restricted unless the deed conveying same shows upon its face that such purchase was made with restricted funds.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "Indian or Indians" implies consultation with tribes or individuals. However, the text only sets a legal condition for land status based on deed language and funding source; it does not require the government to consult with anyone before making a decision.
